title: Philadelphia man sentenced to 41 months for straw purchasing firearms

Philadelphia man sentenced to 41 months for straw purchasing firearms
Deontrae Marquis Jackson has been sentenced to over three years in prison for straw purchasing firearms in Pennsylvania courts after working with others who bought guns on behalf of felons. The prosecution involved multiple agencies as part of broader efforts led by Project Safe Neighborhoods.
Deontrae Marquis Jackson, age 35, of Philadelphia, was sentenced on Oct. 1 to 41 months in prison by United States District Judge Keli M. Neary for straw purchasing firearms, according to the United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Pennsylvania.
According to United States Attorney Brian D. Miller, Jackson worked with others to purchase firearms in the names of women who had no criminal records and were lawfully allowed to buy the firearms. After obtaining the firearms, they were sold or transferred to felons. Between January and February 2021, Jackson and his associates visited federal firearms licensed dealers in Lancaster and York and attempted to purchase seven firearms.
Judge Neary noted that Jackson had a long criminal history involving drug trafficking and firearms offenses. The judge also said that Jackson fled while the case was pending and was later arrested almost two years later by the United States Marshal Service while living in Oregon.
Jackson was found guilty of conspiracy and providing false statements to federally licensed firearms dealers after a three-day bench trial. Co-defendants Alicia Butler-Sanchez and Olivia Johnson pled guilty earlier; both received probationary sentences in 2022 and 2023.
The U.S. Bureau of Alcohol Tobacco Firearms and Explosives investigated this case, which is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Michael A. Consiglio.
The U.S. Attorney for the Middle District of Pennsylvania promotes community safety through initiatives like Project Safe Neighborhoods—an effort coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices nationwide that brings together federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement agencies as well as prosecutors—and re-entry services designed to reduce recidivism among offenders; it serves about 3.2 million residents across a region spanning over 21,900 square miles from facilities including Harrisburg, Scranton, Williamsport, and Wilkes-Barre; handles prosecutions of federal crimes along with civil litigation for the government; operates under the Department of Justice, according to the official website.
